chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
If you are not forbearing, feign forbearance, for it is seldom that a man likens himself to a group and does not become as one of them.

key_terms.أَوْشَكَ: To be about to or likely to
key_terms.تَشَبَّهَ: To resemble or liken oneself to

ai.seo_question: How can one develop the virtue of forbearance if it does not come naturally?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) prescribes the deliberate cultivation of ḥilm (forbearance) as a transformative practice, grounded in the psychological principle that consistent association with virtuous traits leads to their internalization. This advice reflects the Shia emphasis on *taqlid* of character, where conscious effort (*fi'l*) precedes innate disposition (*fitrah*), ensuring that the believer assimilates the qualities of the righteous through sustained emulation.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 207. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
If you cannot forbear, feign to do so because it is seldom that a man likens himself to a group and does not become as one of them. [1]
